newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity closes higher on cool weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity closes higher on cool weather.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures closed mostly higher amid forecasts for cooler weather in the Pacific Northwest, trade sources said Friday.
"The six to 10-day outlook is for below average temperatures in the Northwest," noted one trader.

But he and others said they expected the spread between California-Oregon border (COB) contracts and Palo Verde (PV) contracts to continue to widen as spring approaches and hydropower volumes in the Northwest increase further.
"We might see a bit more strength at PV, but then the units will start to come back and prices will probably fall," said another trader.
In the Southwest, outages continued at a 1,221 MW Palo Verde nuclear unit and a 750 MW Navajo coal-fired unit.
The 1,070 MW San Onofre nuclear unit in California was expected to restart next Friday after a refueling outage that began Nov 30 was extended for additional repair work.
In the Northwest, the 474 MW Hermiston, Ore., was expected to shut Saturday until July, with its generation displaced by lower-cost hydropower.
April COB settled up 8 cents at $9.30 per megawatt hour (MWh), while May was up 15 cents at $9.40.
June COB was down 6 cents at $10.25 and July ended 5 cents lower at $13.25.
PV settled up 25 cents at $13.15 after trading in a narrow range, while May was up 5 cents at $13.70, June was unchanged at $15.00 and July was down 15 cents at $19.45.
NYMEX said an estimated 153 COB and 158 PV contracts traded on Friday.
